record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Develop the realization theory for chiral polytopes: describe and organize their realizations in geometric spaces in a way analogous to the established realization theory for regular polytopes.

evidence.quote: Problem 36 Develop the details of the realization theory for chiral polytopes.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope of rank $n$ is a partially ordered set satisfying the standard axioms (existence of a least and greatest face, the diamond condition, strong flag-connectedness, and a rank function). Its automorphism group acts on the set of flags (maximal chains). An abstract polytope is called regular if this action is transitive on flags, and chiral if it has exactly two orbits on flags with the property that any two adjacent flags lie in different orbits.

A realization of an abstract polytope $\mathcal{P}$ of rank $n$ in a Euclidean space $\mathbb{E}^d$ is a mapping $\beta$ from the vertex set of $\mathcal{P}$ into $\mathbb{E}^d$ together with the induced mappings of higher-rank faces, compatible with incidence; a realization is faithful if these induced mappings are injective on each rank. For regular abstract polytopes there is a well-developed realization theory (organized via the realization cone, the structure of pure/irreducible realizations, the Wythoff-space construction, dimension and full-rank/nearly full-rank bounds, and orthogonal decomposition of realizations).

Problem: Develop an analogous, complete realization theory for chiral abstract polytopes. In particular, describe the space of realizations of a finite (and infinite) chiral abstract polytope of rank $n$ in Euclidean spaces $\mathbb{E}^d$, identify the irreducible/pure realizations and a decomposition theorem for general realizations, determine the minimum dimension required for a faithful realization (full-rank and nearly full-rank cases) and the constraints imposed by chirality (e.g., non-convexity, skewness, mirror behavior), and provide a structural organization of geometric realizations of chiral polytopes parallel to the regular case.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches indicate that while certain dimensional bounds for faithful realizations of chiral polytopes are known (a finite chiral polytope of rank $n$ requires a faithful Euclidean realization of dimension strictly greater than $n$, with full-rank and nearly full-rank realizations studied in low ranks), no comprehensive realization theory analogous to that for regular abstract polytopes has been developed. Recent works treat specific families (e.g., chiral 5-polytopes of full rank, chiral polytopes of type $\{4,4,\ldots,4\}$) but a general structural framework remains to be established.

status_evidence.title: Regular and chiral polytopes in low dimensions
status_evidence.snippet: Studies low-dimensional realizations of chiral polytopes; treats specific cases rather than a general realization theory.
status_evidence.claim: Realization studies of chiral polytopes have so far been case-based in low dimensions.

status_evidence.title: A chiral 5-polytope of full rank
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs a chiral 5-polytope realized faithfully at full rank.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to address specific realization existence problems for chiral polytopes.

status_evidence.title: Realization - Polytope Wiki
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses faithful realizations and notes geometric constraints distinguishing chiral from regular cases.
status_evidence.claim: Faithful realizations of chiral polytopes require strictly higher dimension than the rank, and the general theory remains less developed than for regular polytopes.
